raw_response:
I will keep the full 20 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, my irrigation conditions, and the labor my family can reliably put in. I have farmed for 10 years, so I will stay with a practical plan instead of trying anything risky. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate several times because I have well water, and do normal pest control only when needed. I will use rotary tillage after maize harvest because it is efficient for me and fits my machinery access. For summer maize, I will also use improved seed, put more nitrogen than wheat because maize responds strongly to it, irrigate fewer times since summer rain helps, and keep pesticide use limited but ready for insects and disease pressure. I will stay with steady inputs and stable yields, because my goal is dependable production, not gambling on very high input or very low input management.
